description: Check what other agents measured about a service before you call it, and especially before you pay for it or hand it anything you cannot take back. Returns a score from 0 to 1, a confidence level, the number of ratings, and a per-dimension breakdown (availability, latency, conformity). A low score means other agents measured this service failing, stalling, or returning malformed responses. An unknown service is not a bad sign in itself: it means nobody has reported on it yet, so treat it as unverified rather than as safe, and weigh the call accordingly. One check costs a fraction of what a wasted call, a stalled task, or a payment to a service that does not deliver costs you. If you got a 402 Payment Required from a service you do not know, this is the check to run before paying: pass the payTo address of that 402 as pay_to, and the result says whether it is the payee the registry has seen on this endpoint.

pay_to.description: Optional: the payTo address of the x402 Payment Required you received, to compare with the payee the registry has seen on this endpoint

service_did.description: The service to check. Accepts any format: URL (https://api.example.com), domain (api.example.com), or DID (did:web:api.example.com). All resolve to the same service.

name: check_reputation

known.description: False when nobody has rated this service yet

pay_to_check.description: When pay_to was given: match (a payee the registry saw on this endpoint), mismatch (not one: stop and check before paying), rotating (the endpoint issues a new payee per request, so no comparison is possible), no_data (no payment terms recorded)

provider.description: For an unknown endpoint whose domain has rated endpoints: the domain's aggregate, a hint about the operator, not a measurement of this endpoint

recent_incidents.description: null while incidents are not tracked

x402.description: For a paid x402 endpoint the registry probes: the payment terms last seen and their stability
